name: 03 - Upwork Job Monitor (RSS → Claude fit score → Telegram)

parameters.content:
## 1. Poll & configure

Runs every **15 minutes**.

**Config** (Set node) is the single place to change behaviour:
- `feedUrl` – placeholder; the real feed source is confirmed in a later phase (Upwork RSS availability varies; Vollna or a scraper are alternatives). You can also use `{{ $env.JOBS_FEED_URL }}` if env access is enabled on your instance.
- `keywords` – case-insensitive match against title + description
- `minBudget` – jobs below this (when a budget is detectable) are dropped
- `minFit` – threshold for the Telegram alert
- `telegramChatId` – where alerts go
- `systemPrompt` – the freelancer profile Claude scores against

## 2. Filter, parse budget, dedupe

One Code node does the cheap work *before* we pay for an LLM call:
- keyword filter (any keyword in title/description)
- budget parsing from the HTML description (`Budget: $500` or `Hourly Range: $30-$50`)
- min-budget check
- dedupe with `$getWorkflowStaticData('global').seenGuids` so each job is scored only once (last 2 000 GUIDs kept)

If nothing new matches, the node outputs 0 items and the run ends here.

## 3. Score with Claude

Direct call to the Anthropic Messages API (`claude-opus-5`, `max_tokens` 1024). The system prompt holds a short freelancer profile and asks for strict JSON `{ "fit": 1-10, "reasons": [...] }`.

**Parse Score** extracts the first text block, strips code fences if any, and `JSON.parse`s it. A parse failure yields `fit: 0` with the reason `parse_error` instead of crashing the run.

Node is set to *retry 2x* and *continue on error* (regular output) so one bad response doesn't kill the batch.

## 4. Alert

`fit >= minFit` → Telegram message with title, budget, score, top 2 reasons and the link. Everything else is discarded (NoOp) but still marked as seen, so it will not be re-scored.

assignments.name: systemPrompt
assignments.value:
You are screening freelance job posts for a specific freelancer and must decide how good a fit each post is.

Freelancer profile: n8n / AI automation engineer, Python/TypeScript, 6+ years of backend experience. Builds production n8n workflows, API integrations, webhook pipelines, RAG and LLM-agent automations, and migrations from Zapier/Make.com. Prefers well-scoped projects with a clear business outcome and a budget consistent with senior work; not interested in pure front-end, WordPress theming, data-entry, or jobs that only want a no-code beginner.

Respond with ONLY a JSON object, no prose and no code fences, in exactly this shape:
{"fit": <integer 1-10>, "reasons": ["<short reason>", "<short reason>", "<short reason>"]}

Scoring guide: 9-10 = ideal match in skills, scope and budget; 7-8 = good match with minor concerns; 4-6 = partial match or unclear scope/budget; 1-3 = poor match.
